findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent or empty
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` without checking that a row was returned. On any site where the `embed_category` site setting was never saved (the default is ''), the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and calling `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking deploys. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15. Both lookups need nil checks before indexing.

findings.title: SQL injection / broken migration via unescaped host values in INSERT
findings.body: The migration interpolates each migrated host value directly into a SQL string: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Host values come from the admin-editable `embeddable_hosts` site setting and may contain a single quote (the old setting had no strict validation), which either breaks the migration with a syntax error or allows arbitrary SQL to run during migrate. Use `quote`/sanitize or ActiveRecord inserts with connection quoting instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError when the host id doesn't exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a nonexistent or already-deleted id, and the controller then calls `host.host = ...` (update) or `host.destroy` (destroy) on nil, producing a 500 error instead of a 404. This is easy to hit from the admin UI by double-clicking delete on the same row. Guard for a nil record and return not_found.

findings.title: create/update crash with 500 when embeddable_host params are missing
findings.body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` assumes the nested params hash exists. A PUT/POST request without the `embeddable_host` key (e.g. from an outdated client, a manual API call, or the embedding controller's empty `update({})` payload) raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 rather than a 400/422 validation error. Use `params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(:host, :category_id)` or safe navigation.

findings.title: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op but is wired to the frontend save button
findings.body: The `update` action just re-renders the serialization of freshly loaded data; it never reads or persists any request parameters. The admin UI's `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which PUTs to this route, so the 'save' button silently does nothing. Either implement the update (persist the embedding settings) or remove the PUT route and the save button until it does something.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicate embeddable hosts
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or unique index on `embeddable_hosts.host`, so an admin can create the same host multiple times (also a race between two admins). `record_for_host` then uses `.first`, so the category applied to new embedded topics is nondeterministic among the duplicates. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive, matching the `lower(host) = ?` lookup) and a unique index in the migration.

findings.title: record_for_host compares a possibly mixed-case referer host against lowercased stored hosts
findings.body: The lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` — only the stored side is lowercased. `URI(...).host` preserves the case of the referer (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `EvilTrout.com`), so a referer with uppercase letters fails to match even though the equivalent lowercase referer works. The comparison should be `where("lower(host) = ?", host.to_s.downcase)`.

findings.title: category_id is not validated to reference an existing category
findings.body: The controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly and saves. There is no validation that the category exists (the model only has a format validation on `host`), so an arbitrary integer (or a stale id from the UI after a category was deleted) is stored, and topics embedded from that host will be created in a nonexistent category. Add a presence/existence validation for category.

findings.title: save() leaves the row in edit mode and loses unsaved state feedback on failure paths
findings.body: On save, `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId))` runs only in the success handler, but if `categoryId` is blank (admin cleared the category chooser) `findById(null)` returns undefined and the UI shows an empty category while the server silently falls back to uncategorized — the displayed state does not match what was saved. Additionally the buffered `host` name is never synced back onto the record (`host.save(props)` behavior aside), so cancelling after a failed save can show stale values. Mirror the server's uncategorized fallback or block blank categories client-side.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `category` fabricators. The code works because Fabricator loads all files, but the file names no longer describe their contents, which will confuse future edits (e.g. someone adding a category fabricator to category_fabricator.rb creating a duplicate-definition conflict with the other file). The contents should live in the correctly named files.

findings.title: No functional tests for the new admin controllers' CRUD behavior
findings.body: Both new controller specs only assert the controller's superclass. There are no tests for create/update/destroy, including the nil-record 500s on nonexistent ids, missing-param handling, blank category fallback to uncategorized, or authorization (the routes use AdminConstraint but the controller's own before_filter only requires staff). Since this PR introduces the whole persistence path for embeddable hosts, these behaviors are currently untested.
